findings.title: Look, Don't Load: Model Inspection in Unsloth Studio Leads to Critical Arbitrary Code Execution
findings.summary_md: The original researcher disclosure, published September 29, 2026 by Ariel Fogel of Pillar Security, one day before the story's first_seen. It documents the full mechanism: the Studio backend's load_model_config defaulted trust_remote_code=True, the capability probes at /api/models/config/{model_name:path} and /api/models/check-vision/{model_name:path} inherited it, and a repo config.json auto_map entry pointing AutoConfig at a sibling Python file executed on mere model selection. The post also gives the disclosure timeline (private report early June 2026 via GHSA-pc2m-72c4-r38q, fix commit 0533efe3 on June 18, fix verified in 2026.6.9) and notes the maintainers declined to publish the advisory, so no CVE was assigned.

findings.title: unsloth 2026.6.9 release on PyPI
findings.summary_md: The vendor fix release that closed the vulnerability. The unsloth-2026.6.9 wheel was uploaded to PyPI on 2026-06-22T16:13:03Z, roughly three months before public disclosure, meaning the patch has been available since late June and only environments frozen on earlier wheels remain exposed. PyPI shows 2026.5.10, the last release with the vulnerable Studio path per the researcher, was uploaded 2026-06-01, and the current release is 2026.9.12.

findings.title: Commit 0533efe3: Harden model fetching (#6391)
findings.summary_md: The vendor fix commit, dated June 18, 2026 per the Pillar disclosure timeline. It adds a consent gate that scans a model's auto_map repository code before execution, keeps capability detection code-free by reading raw config.json instead of AutoConfig, adds a picklescan and ClamAV backed malware gate over load paths, and removes the blanket trust remote code toggles from chat and export. The unsloth repo's security advisories tab shows zero published advisories, consistent with the maintainer decision not to publish the GHSA and assign no CVE.
